title: The glide path: step down, not jump off
objectives: Describe an illustrative glide path from three years out to the goal.
Explain why the shift is done in steps through an STP.
body_md:
When the goal is one to three years away, the aim is to protect what has been built so a market fall just before the goal cannot derail it.

## An illustrative path

| Years to goal | Illustrative equity share |
|---|---|
| 3 | About 60–70% |
| 2 | About 40–50% |
| 1 | About 20–30% |
| At goal | Close to 0% for money to be spent |

## How the shift is made

The shift happens in steps, through an STP from the equity fund into a debt or liquid fund, or by redirecting new SIP money into debt. That avoids one big switch on a single day, and it spreads the exit across prices rather than betting on one.

## What to watch

- These shares are illustrative; the actual path depends on the client's risk profile and how flexible the goal is.
- Each STP transfer is a redemption, so check exit loads per instalment and refer tax to a CA.
- Do not stop the whole SIP at once if the client still needs to save; direct the new money to debt instead.
example: Rahul's house down payment is due in 24 months and 80% of the money is in equity. The plan moves about a fifth of the equity to a short-duration fund every quarter, checks the exit load on recent instalments, and leaves the rest invested until the last year.
say: We'll step down to debt over the next two years, not jump off in one day.
The point is to protect the goal from a fall, not to predict one.
never: Let's switch everything to debt tomorrow.
A glide path means we can time the market.

check.q: Which is the illustrative glide path for a goal three, two and one year away?
check.why: Equity steps down as the goal approaches: about 65%, 45%, 25%, and close to 0% at the goal for money to be spent.

o: A gradual, stepped shift from equity to debt as the goal nears
Moving all the money on one day
Selling everything when the goal arrives
Switching funds every year for higher returns
check.why: It is a stepped shift over one to three years, not one big switch.

check.q: How is the shift usually made?
o: By redeeming everything on the goal date
Through an STP into a debt or liquid fund, or by sending new SIP money to debt
By taking a loan against the units
By moving to another equity fund
check.why: An STP or redirecting new SIP money spreads the move across prices instead of betting on one day.
